messages.subject: mapping percentage going backwards
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering what causes the mapping percentage to go back from 100% back down again to a number less than that...before finally completing a job.

The function I am using is as follows:

hadooplapply <- function(vec,fun.string,...){
suppressPackageStartupMessages(require(rmr2))
values(from.dfs(mapreduce(
  input=scatter(to.dfs(vec)),
  map=function(k,v){keyval(k,lapply(X=v,FUN=match.fun(fun.string),...))},
  verbose=TRUE)))
}

the fun.string is a function that is being called and is being applied. My initial thoughts are that since it uses some mclapply functions...that this is what causes the percentages to go backwards sometimes....

but either way...options can be set to prevent it from using mclapply type functions, which actually speed up the overall times....the mclapply function basically pulls out samples from a large data set and calculates means.

i know that the first mapping and reducing is due to the scatter function being used on the input....but what is odd about the below example is that for the actual function, it gets to 100% for the map percentage reasonably quickly... but then hangs around before it goes back down and reaches 100% again

can you let me know what might be going on here, has this been seen before....the function output is as follows:

I not that you are using dev, I would recommend not to do that while still learning the package, dev can be broken at times, it's not tested at every push. 


Antonio

parts:
Do you think that the temporary memory failures could be due to a call to mclapply? has this been a problem in the past?

i.e. does calling a function that uses forking/multicore-same-machine parallelisation cause problems once introduced into a mapreduce format?

i.e. if a function that is called, detects the number of available cores and then uses them all, to carry out another function, would this cause problems?

i.e. does having multi-leveled parallelisation i.e. hadoop level parallelisation and multicore level parallelisation at the same time cause problems?

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#453] mapping percentage going backwards
parts:
On Tuesday, 11 December 2012 09:34:56 UTC+11, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:



On Mon, Dec 10, 2012 at 2:17 PM, Hideyoshi Maeda <hideyos...@gmail.com> wrote:
Do you think that the temporary memory failures could be due to a call to mclapply? has this been a problem in the past?
 
i.e. does calling a function that uses forking/multicore-same-machine parallelisation cause problems once introduced into a mapreduce format?

You are the trailblazer on this.
weird...would have expected other people to have done this before me!

i.e. if a function that is called, detects the number of available cores and then uses them all, to carry out another function, would this cause problems?

I can see the potential problems of having to overlapping parallelism layers completely unaware of each other.
is there a way perhaps to just split the list across the machines only...and then the function works just on the given part of the list on that machine?

i.e. does having multi-leveled parallelisation i.e. hadoop level parallelisation and multicore level parallelisation at the same time cause problems?

Imagine if  mclapply is called at the same time on all the cores on one machine. I wouldn't want to be in the same building with it.
would your general advice be to let hadoop deal with the parallelisation and not add in multiple layers of parallelisation?

On Tuesday, 11 December 2012 02:37:49 UTC+11, Antonio Piccolboni wrote:
Hi
You are having temporary failures. Your tasks are failing and being retried and they eventually succeed after multiple attempts. It could be  a non deterministic behavior in your code or one misconfigured node. I not that you are using dev, I would recommend not to do that while still learning the package, dev can be broken at times, it's not tested at every push. 


Antonio


On Mon, Dec 10, 2012 at 12:06 AM, Hideyoshi Maeda <hideyos...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi,

I was wondering what causes the mapping percentage to go back from 100% back down again to a number less than that...before finally completing a job.

The function I am using is as follows:

hadooplapply <- function(vec,fun.string,...){
suppressPackageStartupMessages(require(rmr2))
values(from.dfs(mapreduce(
  input=scatter(to.dfs(vec)),
  map=function(k,v){keyval(k,lapply(X=v,FUN=match.fun(fun.string),...))},
  verbose=TRUE)))
}

the fun.string is a function that is being called and is being applied. My initial thoughts are that since it uses some mclapply functions...that this is what causes the percentages to go backwards sometimes....

but either way...options can be set to prevent it from using mclapply type functions, which actually speed up the overall times....the mclapply function basically pulls out samples from a large data set and calculates means.

i know that the first mapping and reducing is due to the scatter function being used on the input....but what is odd about the below example is that for the actual function, it gets to 100% for the map percentage reasonably quickly... but then hangs around before it goes back down and reaches 100% again

can you let me know what might be going on here, has this been seen before....the function output is as follows:
